What to do: Document audience, geography/language, seed keywords, competing URLs, and current visibility before coding.
Done when: Audience, market/language, competitor URLs, and baseline visibility are written down.
Tools: Search; Ahrefs/Semrush or manual SERP review; competitor sites
Review cadence: Once before build; refresh at 90 days
Notes: Purpose: relevance/ranking consideration; measurement. Important strategy input, but not a universal cutover blocker. Operating design; no external ranking claim. Related controls: 0.2, 0.3, 0.4.

What to do: Map priority search landing pages to their main user need, relevant query cluster, intent and business role before architecture decisions. Include navigational intent where relevant. Assign other URL patterns their functional purpose and indexability decision under 0.3. Document a meaningful outcome where useful rather than forcing every URL into a conversion target.
Done when: Priority search pages have a documented purpose and query/intent mapping. Utility, private and other functional routes are accounted for in 0.3 without artificial keyword or conversion assignments. Use the mapping to guide architecture and content decisions, then refine it with actual search evidence after launch.
Tools: Keyword research tools; Search Console later
Review cadence: Once before build; update when adding pages
Notes: Purpose: relevance/ranking consideration. C01. Strategy and relevance planning; P1 and nongating. The URL-purpose/indexability contract remains in 0.3. Source: Helpful content. Source IDs: SRC033.

Task: Information architecture, URL inventory and indexability matrix
What to do: Inventory planned CMS, API-generated and uploaded URL patterns before implementation, including public indexable pages, excluded search/tag/filter/feed/file patterns and private routes. Record template, intent, parent/discovery links, status, indexability/directives, canonical, sitemap decision, locale and launch criticality. Reconcile to actual routes and uploaded assets.
Done when: The approved matrix covers every planned pattern and priority URL, including intentional exclusions and non-HTML files. Each has consistent status, access, indexing, canonical and discovery rules; private data requires authorization.
Tools: Spreadsheet / repo doc
Review cadence: Update whenever a page type is added
Notes: Purpose: indexing/discovery; security/governance. C05. The matrix drives later QA. robots.txt does not make data private or guarantee removal. Sources: Robots meta and X-Robots-Tag; Googlebot fetch limits. Source IDs: SRC009; SRC010; SRC040; SRC045; SRC103.

What to do: Approve the measurement purpose, business outcomes, reporting owner and chosen tools, or a documented no-tracking decision. For selected instrumentation define events/key events, trigger and deduplication rules, attribution scope and expected collection or suppression by consent/journey state. Specify required receipt evidence and reporting latency. Link the qualified privacy/vendor decision in 0.9 and record measurement limitations before implementation.
Done when: A dated owner decision defines the measurement scope and success criteria, including any no-tracking choice. Selected events, consent expectations, validation methods and review owners are explicit. Resolve 2.5, 2.6, 4.7 and 5.6 independently from that scope; no tool, conversion event or cross-product association is required merely to complete this plan.
Tools: Measurement plan; privacy/vendor decisions; chosen-platform documentation
Notes: Purpose: measurement; security/governance. C12. Measurement is a business/governance control, not a ranking requirement. A no-analytics choice does not decide consent for other tags or vendors. Sources: Google Consent Mode; Search Console and GA4 linking. Source IDs: SRC004; SRC068.

Applies to: Sites documenting organization/person identity and relevant official profiles
What to do: Record the actual public brand and relevant legal identity, logo and official profiles that already exist or serve a real business purpose. Verify what entity each URL identifies and who controls or maintains it where relevant. Use sameAs only for a page that unambiguously identifies the same entity. Do not create irrelevant profiles merely to complete this checklist.
Done when: The identity record uses accurate names and relevant verified references. Selected sameAs URLs identify the same entity, not a related company, topic or product. Differences between legal and public brand names are intentional. Optional profile or schema adoption is not required, and no entity-recognition or ranking outcome is promised.
Tools: Brand doc; social/profile accounts
Notes: Purpose: security/governance; optional enhancement. C25. Optional identity governance and markup support. sameAs can refer to authoritative identity pages as well as controlled profiles; ownership is not the sole test. Source: Schema.org sameAs. Source IDs: SRC078.

Applies to: Sites deciding how their content is used by AI search and training systems
Task: AI crawler, AI-feature and training policy
What to do: If an explicit AI-use policy is needed, maintain one provider/purpose register with owner, source/version date, scope, business reason and allow/block/limit decision. Separate ordinary Google crawl/index/preview rules, Search Console Search generative AI inclusion, Google-Extended, and each selected provider's search, training and user-directed fetch agents. Record the effective Search Console setting and any inherited parent or child override. Use current product documentation; do not assume one provider's robots behavior applies to another.
Done when: Each selected control has a resolved purpose/scope decision and dated implementation evidence or a clearly recorded pending action. Google Search AI inclusion is separate from training and does not change ranking/inclusion in other Search parts. Record actual account access and inherited scope. Optional services and experimental files are not mandatory launch requirements, and no setting is presented as a universal AI opt-out.
Tools: Search Console Settings > Search generative AI; robots.txt; CDN/WAF rules; Sources sheet
Review cadence: Before selected policy takes effect; after provider/scope changes; review quarterly
Notes: Purpose: security/governance; optional enhancement. H01/H02. Checked 2026-09-09: dedicated Google help announces worldwide rollout on 2026-08-31; verify the actual property. Google-Extended is a robots product token, not an HTTP user agent, and covers its documented Gemini training/grounding uses. llms.txt remains optional/experimental; Google Search ignores it for visibility/ranking. Sources: Search AI control; Google common crawlers; Google AI optimization. Source IDs: SRC002; SRC018; SRC037; SRC084; SRC085; SRC086.

Task: International market, localization and URL strategy
What to do: Research needs per intended locale; choose stable folders, subdomains or ccTLDs and assign localization owners. Plan canonical/hreflang relationships, available page equivalents and localized journeys. Keep valuable translations independently indexable; document any preferred canonical for same-language regional duplicates. Provide user-controlled locale links instead of forced IP or browser-language redirects.
Done when: Each launch locale has demand/user-need evidence, an owner, URL/content plan and approved canonical/hreflang and journey decisions. Same-language consolidation is justified explicitly; distinct translations are not collapsed to one language. Users and crawlers can reach intended variants.
Tools: hreflang tester; GSC
Notes: Purpose: indexing/discovery; relevance/ranking consideration. C07. Plan regional differences deliberately; localization does not require identical offers in every market. Source: International sites; Localized versions / hreflang. Source IDs: SRC012; SRC013.

Applies to: Migration / redesign / URL change; inherited or previously used domain
What to do: Record URL-move and domain-history scope separately. For inherited domains, inspect available GSC manual actions, security issues and prior URL removals during discovery and recheck before cutover. For moves, inventory pages/assets, important links and available traffic/ranking baselines; approve URL outcomes, content parity, freeze/DNS timing, recovery owners and old-domain continuity. Plan redirects for at least one year and an eligible Change of Address property matrix.
Done when: History findings, access limitations and required remedies are recorded; unresolved required checks or blocking inherited issues fail. For moves, the complete inventory/map, baseline limitations, cutover/freeze plan, recovery reference and redirect/domain-retention owner are approved before build completion and current at cutover. A history-only case records that no URL move applies; it does not require redirects or Change of Address.
Tools: URL inventory/map; GSC reports and property matrix; recovery runbook
Notes: Purpose: indexing/discovery; security/governance. C21/F01. Change of Address excludes protocol-only, same-domain www, hosting-only and same-domain path moves. Eligible moves require the same Google account to own old/new properties; source scope excludes paths and does not include child subdomains automatically. Include verified source variants, including www/non-www, even when inactive. Sources: Google site moves; Change of Address; Manual actions; Security issues. Source IDs: SRC011; SRC059; SRC060; SRC061.

Task: Legal, privacy, consent and accessibility scope decision
What to do: Document jurisdictions, business model, audience, data collection, required legal/consumer information and consent approach. Record accessibility obligations or exemptions with qualified review where needed. Specify the adopted WCAG version/level, pages and complete journeys assessed, supported technology scope, and which access/obligation requirements block release. Separate an assessment from any conformance claim.
Done when: A dated scope decision identifies applicable requirements and evidence, owners and qualified escalation. The accessibility target and blocking criteria are explicit. Legal applicability/exemptions are supported by the appropriate review; SEO completion is not legal sign-off or proof of conformance.
Tools: Legal scope checklist; Sources sheet
Review cadence: Before design/build; revisit when scope changes
Notes: Purpose: legal/accessibility; security/governance. C19. Accessibility and obligation scope protects users and delivery decisions. Record the actual required target; do not assume one WCAG version or a legal exemption applies universally. Sources: WCAG 2.2; Accessibility evaluation. Source IDs: SRC014; SRC015.

What to do: Choose rendering for the intended crawlers. Prefer server-delivered critical content as a reliability policy; SSR/SSG is not a universal Google requirement. Test initial and rendered metadata, content and links, resource/API access, hydration, deep links and missing-page behavior without user interaction. Record and justify meaningful differences against the URL matrix.
Done when: Every indexable template exposes required content and crawlable links to intended crawlers. Raw/rendered directives and canonicals do not conflict; initial noindex is absent on approved indexable pages. Resource failures and missing routes are tested. Required output stays inside the verified fetch envelope in 1.5.
Tools: curl; View Source; URL Inspection
Notes: Purpose: indexing/discovery. C02/D01. Successful browser rendering alone does not prove every crawler can render. Sources: JavaScript SEO basics; JavaScript troubleshooting; Googlebot fetch limits. Source IDs: SRC038; SRC039; SRC040.

What to do: Use real a href links, semantic landmarks, one clear primary page heading and a logical heading hierarchy. Do not treat a strict single-H1 rule as a ranking requirement.
Done when: Priority URLs are reachable through normal links; landmarks, link purpose and heading hierarchy are usable by crawlers and assistive technology.
Tools: HTML validator; Screaming Frog
Notes: Purpose: indexing/discovery; legal/accessibility. Source IDs: SRC014; SRC103.

What to do: Document descriptive, stable URL paths and host/slash/parameter conventions. Preserve meaningful case-sensitive paths. For equivalent duplicates choose a permanent 301/308 redirect, or document an intentional 200 duplicate with consistent canonical signals. Align internal links and sitemaps with the preferred accessible, indexable URL; use self-canonicals where appropriate.
Done when: Sampled variants follow the approved mapping. Retained 200 duplicates have a justified canonical policy; targets work and are indexable. No conflicting signals, loops or accidental duplicates exist on priority patterns. Controlled redirects use one hop where feasible; external chains are assessed by impact.
Tools: curl -I; Screaming Frog; Search Console
Notes: Purpose: indexing/discovery. C03. Canonical declarations express a preference, not guaranteed selection. Sources: Canonicalization; Redirects and Google Search; URL structure. Source IDs: SRC010; SRC024; SRC041.

What to do: Test successful responses, permanent/temporary redirects, missing/removed URLs, internal search, invalid facets/pagination and application failures. Use 404/410 for genuinely absent resources, 503 for temporary service unavailability and 429 for deliberate throttling. Follow the indexability matrix for valid search-result states, normally 200 with noindex. Never mask application failures as indexable 200 pages.
Done when: Representative responses match the matrix. Valid empty search states are distinguished from nonexistent/error-like URLs and invalid facets. Missing resources return genuine errors with useful UX; no unintended soft 404, redirect loop or indexable error response remains. Excluded search states stay out of ordinary sitemaps.
Tools: curl -I; Screaming Frog; server logs
Notes: Purpose: indexing/discovery. C04. A temporary outage is not a permanent removal. Correct status handling does not make an active production outage acceptable. Sources: HTTP status codes; Faceted navigation. Source IDs: SRC042; SRC043.

Task: Performance acceptance criteria, diagnostics and fetch budgets
What to do: Before testing, classify per-template LCP, CLS, TBT, asset/request and TTFB budgets as launch thresholds or diagnostics. Freeze devices, network, cache state, journeys and repeat/summary method. Expose the LCP resource promptly without lazy-loading it. Separately measure each uncompressed document/resource against current crawler limits and a margin. Test fonts, fallback metrics, required glyphs, layout shifts and delivery of changed cached assets.
Done when: The versioned policy identifies each launch threshold, diagnostic target, test profile and owner. Templates meet current acceptance criteria and per-file fetch limits. Required text/glyphs remain usable during font delay/failure; changed cached assets reach returning users. Diagnostic overruns have impact, owner and due date. A failed criterion remains failed until corrected or formally revised and retested; an exception alone cannot pass the gate.
Tools: Lighthouse CI; WebPageTest; PageSpeed Insights; bundle analyzer
Notes: Purpose: measurement; security/governance. C08/D01/D05. TBT is a lab diagnostic, not field INP. Keep crawler byte limits separate from total page weight and project budgets: Googlebot Search verified 2026-09-08 at 2 MB per non-PDF and 64 MB per PDF, uncompressed, with separate CSS/JS fetches. Font subsets need permission and required glyphs; system fonts are valid. Sources: Web Vitals metrics; Googlebot fetch limits; Font performance; HTTP cache and versioned assets. Source IDs: SRC006; SRC040; SRC048; SRC049; SRC053; SRC093.

What to do: Serve the preferred production origin over valid HTTPS. Redirect controlled HTTP and equivalent non-preferred hosts permanently with appropriate 301/308 responses. Document any intentional retained duplicate-host exception and its canonical/access policy. Test certificate coverage, mixed content and each controlled variant.
Done when: Certificates and HTTPS responses are valid, with no mixed content. Controlled equivalent variants reach the intended destination without loops, preferably in one hop. Any retained duplicate or unavoidable external chain has reviewed evidence and consistent canonical behavior.
Tools: curl; SSL test; crawler
Notes: Purpose: indexing/discovery; security/governance. C03. Distinct sites or meaningful routes must not be blindly collapsed. Sources: Canonicalization; Redirects and Google Search. Source IDs: SRC010; SRC041.

Task: Infrastructure, cache policy and monitoring design
What to do: Document actual hosting/CDN layers, cache keys and bypass/revalidation rules, compression, appropriate security headers and protocol choices. Cover public, excluded, private, locale and cookie/header variants. Plan invalidation and versioned assets. Inventory third-party scripts with owners and budgets. Assign monitoring owners, response targets and log needs before launch; implement and prove readiness in 4.2/4.12.
Done when: Infrastructure and script choices have accountable owners and testable policies. Private responses are not shared across users; public indexing signals remain consistent through caches and edge rules. Conditional components and absent layers are explicitly recorded. Required preflight evidence is linked from 4.2 and 4.12.
Tools: Hosting/CDN configuration; browser network tools; HTTP probes; alert routing and runbook
Notes: Purpose: security/governance. D05/F03. Implementation and risk control, not a requirement to use a CDN or HTTP/3. Private/no-store caching rules do not replace authorization. Critical access/privacy failures block 4.2; missing monitoring readiness blocks 4.12. Sources: HTTP caching standard; HTTP cache and versioned assets; Monitoring distributed systems. Source IDs: SRC047; SRC048; SRC050; SRC051.

What to do: Password-protect or IP-restrict staging and preview environments. Use environment-conditional robots/meta controls as defense in depth and automated tests to ensure staging noindex rules cannot ship to production.
Done when: Staging and preview environments require effective access control. For production, every URL pattern approved as indexable is crawlable and has no unintended noindex in the response headers or HTML. Every intentionally excluded public pattern retains the approved indexing directives, and every private pattern retains effective authorization. The environment-specific URL matrix, including both indexable and excluded examples, matches the observed raw and rendered behavior. The preflight evidence proves these rules on the release candidate; the applicable launch-day checks confirm them on production after cutover.
Tools: Host auth/basic auth; env vars; robots.txt; meta robots; Search Console
Notes: Purpose: indexing/discovery; security/governance. Do not remove intentional noindex from internal-search or other deliberately excluded public pages. Robots.txt is not confidentiality or guaranteed deindexing; preserve crawl access where needed to read a relied-upon noindex. Production verification belongs to the live checks in Phase 5. Test both allowed and excluded patterns; never treat a clean indexable homepage as proof for the whole matrix. Source IDs: SRC009; SRC038; SRC094.

Applies to: Sites with meaningful images or video
What to do: Compress media, generate responsive sizes, set dimensions or aspect-ratio, use modern formats, lazy-load only below-fold media and provide captions/transcripts or alternatives where required.
Done when: Representative templates serve appropriately sized media without layout shift; the LCP asset is not lazy-loaded; accessibility alternatives are present.
Tools: Image CDN/build pipeline; PageSpeed
Notes: Purpose: indexing/discovery; legal/accessibility. v4: conditional launch gate when media ships. Source IDs: SRC014; SRC098; SRC106; SRC107.

What to do: Block release for unintended noindex on approved indexable patterns, unintended crawler blocks, conflicting canonicals and broken critical internal links. Run automated checks in CI for relevant changes where supported; otherwise use an equivalent repeatable CMS release check with recorded results and an accountable release owner.
Done when: Seeded unintended-noindex, canonical, crawler-access and critical-link defects are detected and prevent the affected release until corrected. Approved exclusions remain intact. A clean release passes the same repeatable check; the evidence identifies the build or CMS revision.
Tools: CI / browser assertions / crawler; documented CMS release QA
Review cadence: Every relevant change and release; review rules quarterly
Notes: Purpose: indexing/discovery; security/governance. C02. This is a project release safeguard, not a Google requirement to use CI or a specific framework. Sources: JavaScript SEO basics; Robots meta and X-Robots-Tag. Source IDs: SRC009; SRC038.

What to do: Add broader checks for duplicate or missing metadata, heading quality, all internal links, schema validation, asset budgets and accessibility regressions without blocking releases on noisy rules until thresholds are proven.
Done when: Rules have owners, low false-positive rates and documented severity; high-confidence failures can be promoted to launch gates later.
Tools: Lighthouse CI; crawler; Playwright; axe; test runner
Notes: Purpose: measurement; security/governance. Operating design; no external ranking claim. Related controls: 1.10, 4.5, 4.6, 4.4.

What to do: Choose useful indexable filter combinations. Define deterministic parameter order and bound discovery of unwanted combinations. Test repeated/invalid parameters, no-result or nonsensical combinations and out-of-range pages. Use real 404 responses for nonexistent states; keep crawl restrictions separate from deindexing and canonicalization decisions.
Done when: Approved filter pages are useful, accessible and linked. Unwanted combinations do not create uncontrolled crawl paths or enter ordinary sitemaps. Negative fixtures return the documented errors. Any noindex relied on for removal remains readable; robots blocking is justified separately.
Tools: Screaming Frog; GSC
Notes: Purpose: indexing/discovery. C06. Source: Faceted navigation. Test absent results and duplicate filters at their actual URLs; do not redirect all such states to one common error URL. Source IDs: SRC043.

What to do: Give listing pages stable distinct URLs and sequential anchor links beneath load-more/infinite-scroll interfaces. Links and item discovery must work for intended crawlers without clicking controls or scrolling. Prefer server-delivered links for reliability; test any rendered-link approach. Give distinct paginated content its own canonical URL.
Done when: Page 2+ and important items are discoverable through crawlable links with valid hrefs. URLs load directly and use intentional canonicals, not blanket page-1 canonicals or fragment-only page numbers. Nonexistent pages and repeated parameters pass the negative tests in 1.12/1.4.
Tools: curl; crawler
Notes: Purpose: indexing/discovery. C02/C06. Source: Pagination. Server rendering is a reliability choice; discoverability and correct output for the intended crawler are the acceptance requirement. Source IDs: SRC044.

What to do: Implement stable locale URLs with localized visible content and accurate HTML lang, including language changes where required by the accessibility target. Use supported hreflang codes and fully qualified URLs with self/return references for intended equivalents. Align canonicals with 0.7, including reviewed same-language regional consolidation. Use x-default only for the chosen unmatched-language fallback; keep switching user controlled.
Done when: Distinct translations remain accessible and indexable; any regional duplicate consolidation matches the approved plan. Hreflang, canonicals, language declarations and switching are consistent. No forced routing hides variants, no alternate points to an unavailable or unrelated page, and the chosen fallback behaves as intended.
Tools: Crawler; hreflang validator; Sources sheet
Notes: Purpose: indexing/discovery; legal/accessibility. C07. Google determines page language from visible content; accurate lang supports assistive technology. Hreflang does not replace translation or justify cross-language canonical collapse. Sources: International sites; Localized versions / hreflang; Declaring language in HTML. Source IDs: SRC012; SRC013; SRC057.

Task: Product URL, variant and lifecycle architecture
What to do: Choose one stable canonical rule per product and variant; keep useful out-of-stock URLs available; define discontinued-product handling, categories, filters, pagination and internal links before catalogue routes ship.
Done when: Variant URLs do not create uncontrolled duplicates; product states have intentional status, canonical, sitemap and internal-link rules.
Tools: URL inventory; crawler; catalogue specification
Notes: Purpose: indexing/discovery; security/governance. Source IDs: SRC010; SRC011; SRC042; SRC074.

Applies to: Sites serving public or private non-HTML files
What to do: Inventory uploaded/generated PDFs, feeds and other non-HTML patterns whether indexable, intentionally excluded or private. Record expected HTTP status, indexing, supported X-Robots-Tag/Link canonical and discovery links. Keep exclusion directives crawl-readable while relying on them; use authorization for private files.
Done when: Headers and access tests cover every important non-HTML pattern. Intended public exclusions and indexable resources follow the matrix; private files cannot be fetched without authorization. Canonical headers are used only where supported and appropriate, with working targets.
Tools: curl -I; crawler; Sources sheet
Review cadence: Before file templates or downloads ship
Notes: Purpose: indexing/discovery; security/governance. C05. Applicability depends on serving files, not on wanting them indexed. Sources: Robots meta and X-Robots-Tag; Canonicalization. Source IDs: SRC009; SRC010.

What to do: Define a deployable recovery target, required backups, recovery owner, cutover window, DNS/CDN dependencies and measurable triggers for availability, indexability and in-scope conversions. For first launch, choose a known-good deployable state or approved holding mode. For an existing site, preserve the prior release and required content/data state. Set recovery-time and acceptable-data-loss targets, including treatment of writes made after cutover.
Done when: The owner has a usable recovery procedure, required access and recoverable assets/data. The first-launch or existing-site target and timing/data-loss limits are approved. Any holding mode has a defined duration, owner and expected response/indexing behavior. Schedule the timed rehearsal in 4.12; a plan alone is not restoration proof.
Tools: Hosting platform; backup system; runbook
Review cadence: Before launch; test after platform changes
Notes: Purpose: security/governance. F04. A new site need not invent a previous release. Restoration and controlled holding behavior protect availability and data; they are operational controls. Baseline data limitations are recorded in 4.11. Source: Contingency planning and recovery testing. Source IDs: SRC063.

Task: Domain registration, ownership and renewal continuity
What to do: Record the registrar, registrant/organization owner, renewal method, expiry date, recovery contacts and privileged access. Enable auto-renew where appropriate, registrar/transfer lock, MFA and monitored billing/recovery paths. For migrations, keep old domains under control for at least as long as redirects are retained.
Done when: Production and any migration-source domains have a named owner, working recovery path, protected registrar access and no near-term expiry/renewal risk; old-domain retention matches the migration plan.
Tools: Registrar account; password manager; domain monitoring
Review cadence: Before launch; verify quarterly and before migrations
Notes: Purpose: security/governance. New in v4.3. Domain expiry is a continuity failure that DNS/SSL monitoring cannot prevent. Source IDs: SRC011; SRC063.

Applies to: Sites running A/B tests, personalization or experiments
Task: SEO-safe testing, personalization and alternate experiences
What to do: Design experiments so users and crawlers are not intentionally shown deceptive content. For alternate test URLs, use a canonical to the original when appropriate; use temporary redirects for short-lived redirect tests; keep core content and crawl paths available; end experiments when the decision is made rather than leaving variants indefinitely.
Done when: Experiment routing, canonicals/redirects and crawl behavior are documented; no cloaking pattern or permanent duplicate variant is created; test retirement has an owner/date.
Tools: Experiment platform; browser/curl; crawler; Search Console
Review cadence: Before each experiment; remove after decision
Notes: Purpose: indexing/discovery; security/governance. New in v4.3. Conditional guidance for experimentation-heavy sites. See Sources: website testing. Source IDs: SRC027.

What to do: Record the sitemap decision in the URL/indexability plan: sitemaps are useful discovery aids, especially for new or complex sites, but are not a universal indexing prerequisite. If used, validate UTF-8, escaping, absolute URLs and meaningful lastmod; split beyond 50,000 URLs or 50 MB uncompressed per sitemap. Ordinary sitemaps list intended canonical, indexable 200 URLs; document migration exceptions separately. Whether sitemaps are used or omitted, verify crawlable internal discovery against the inventory and test robots.txt GET, host/protocol/port and agent scope, UTF-8, 500 KiB parsing boundary, caching and error responses.
Done when: The approved use/omission decision and internal-discovery checks are evidenced. Any implemented sitemap files and referenced URLs pass encoding, limit, status, directive and canonical checks. No priority route/resource is accidentally blocked. Excluded search/filter/tag/file patterns have consistent rules. robots.txt behavior, including intentional absence and cache/error cases, is recorded; reliance on noindex is crawl-readable and private access uses authorization.
Tools: Sitemap validator; Search Console
Notes: Purpose: indexing/discovery. D02/C05. Sources: Sitemap construction; robots.txt interpretation; Site moves. Missing robots.txt is an explicit policy decision, not automatic deindexing. Defaults reflect ordinary launch sitemaps, not temporary migration diagnostics. E02: retain the access/indexability gate; an approved sitemap omission is allowed. Source: Sitemap use decision. Source IDs: SRC045; SRC046; SRC096.

Applies to: Sites with on-page images or image-based controls
What to do: Give meaningful images accurate alternative text based on their purpose; give decorative images empty alt. Avoid keyword stuffing and do not duplicate adjacent captions unnecessarily.
Done when: Priority content images communicate the same purpose without sight; decorative assets are silent to assistive technology.
Tools: Screaming Frog; WCAG check
Notes: Purpose: legal/accessibility. v4: separates accessibility-critical alt handling from low-impact filenames. E02: resolve the actual image inventory, including functional and decorative images. An image-free site can use an approved exclusion; shipped image barriers still require correction. Source: Image text alternatives. Source IDs: SRC098.

Applies to: Sites where image search, Discover or image-rich search appearance matters
What to do: Keep important images discoverable at stable URLs, with useful surrounding text and filenames where practical. Use an image sitemap when it improves discovery. For selected Discover pages, provide relevant high-quality imagery. Google's recommendations are at least 1,200 px wide, more than 300,000 total pixels and a useful 16:9 presentation. Preserve the subject when cropping; select representative og:image or supported schema imagery and permit large previews where rights/policy allow.
Done when: Important images are crawlable and discoverable. Selected pages have a representative image and intentional preview controls. Record decisions against the Discover image recommendations; do not treat them as universal indexability requirements or require special Discover markup. Check rendered crops and avoid generic logos or text-heavy thumbnails where inappropriate.
Tools: CMS/media pipeline; image sitemap; page metadata; robots meta
Notes: Purpose: search-feature eligibility; optional enhancement. H06. Optional media enhancement. Discover eligibility is assessed separately in 2.16; image quality does not guarantee selection. Source: Discover. Source IDs: SRC025.

What to do: Verify the appropriate production property using a durable supported method independent of optional analytics. Prefer a Domain property when DNS control is available; use a correctly scoped URL-prefix property where needed. Record an accountable verified owner, secured recovery and appropriate backup access where feasible. Keep valid verification tokens in place, avoid overwriting other owners' tokens and grant monitoring staff the permissions they need. Document the intended sitemap URL.
Done when: The property covers the intended production URLs and an accountable verified owner can access it. Monitoring permissions and recovery are documented, with backup access where feasible; two owners are not compulsory and shared credentials are not a substitute. Verification remains valid independently of optional tags. Pending setup stays recorded as pending, with an owner and next action; it is not a ranking or website-launch prerequisite.
Tools: Search Console; supported ownership method; access/recovery record
Notes: Purpose: measurement. C14. Recommended monitoring setup, P1/nongating. Domain and URL-prefix properties have different scope and verification options. The live technical requirements in 5.4 remain gates; account setup or report availability is not an indexing guarantee. Sources: Search Console property types; Verify site ownership. Source IDs: SRC087; SRC088.

Applies to: Sites using analytics or conversion measurement
What to do: Implement only the approved 0.4 instrumentation. Configure ownership, timezone, retention, test/internal traffic and applicable values, currency, cross-domain/referral handling. Choose one route/pageview emission method and prevent duplicate triggers. Use safe unique transaction IDs where relevant; remove prohibited payload fields before transmission. If GA4/Search Console linking is selected, match page scope and web stream, permissions and reporting ownership.
Done when: Collection, suppression, values and attribution match the approved state matrix. Expected events are neither missing nor duplicated; relevant transactions reconcile with test records. SPA routes carry current page/referrer data, required cross-domain identifiers survive redirects, and prohibited data is absent from inspected payloads. The optional GA4/Search Console link is correctly scoped if chosen; its absence does not fail this gate.
Tools: Chosen analytics debugger; browser network tools; tag debugger; Search Console Associations
Review cadence: Before launch and after tracking changes
Notes: Purpose: measurement; legal/accessibility. C12/D06. Check live payloads and recipient diagnostics, not only tag configuration. GA4 purchase deduplication needs a nonempty unique transaction_id without customer-identifying data; do not reuse IDs across orders/users or assume all event types are deduplicated. Sources: GA4 SPA measurement; GA4 transaction IDs; GA4 cross-domain measurement; Analytics PII prevention; Search Console and GA4 linking. Source IDs: SRC065; SRC066; SRC067; SRC068; SRC069.

Applies to: Sites where consent is required and/or Google tags use Consent Mode
Task: Consent platform and Google Consent Mode configuration
What to do: Implement the qualified 0.9 privacy decision for the actual regions, vendors and data. Where Google Consent Mode is selected, record Basic/Advanced mode and affected consent types, including ad_user_data/ad_personalization where applicable. Set approved defaults before configuration/events; update choices before navigation and persist/restore them as designed. Test first visit, accept, reject, partial consent, withdrawal and return visits at network/storage level.
Done when: Tag loading, transmission and storage match the approved policy in every required state, including delayed banner/tag loading. Basic blocks Google data until consent; Advanced denied states may send documented cookieless measurements only where approved. Choice changes and withdrawal affect subsequent behavior correctly, denied paths remain usable, and unapproved disclosure or unresolved scope fails.
Tools: CMP; Tag Assistant; browser storage/network tools; Sources sheet
Review cadence: Before launch and after CMP/tag changes
Notes: Purpose: legal/accessibility; security/governance. C13. The chosen mode must fit the qualified policy; Consent Mode is a signal mechanism, not legal certification. No cookies does not mean no transmission. Existing stored data and any deletion obligations need their own approved handling. Sources: Google Consent Mode; Consent Mode implementation timing. Source IDs: SRC004; SRC064.

Applies to: Templates eligible for useful structured data
What to do: For each marked template record vocabulary, supported format, intended consumer/feature, required and recommended properties, content source and maintenance owner. Prefer JSON-LD; accept supported Microdata/RDFa. Decide relevant Organization, LocalBusiness, Article, Product/ProductGroup, VideoObject, paywall, BreadcrumbList and other types using current feature guidance. Describe actual page/entity content; do not generate empty boilerplate entities or infer Google support from Schema.org validity.
Done when: The matrix distinguishes valid vocabulary from each selected feature's eligibility and records required-property results and recommended-property decisions. Shipped markup is accurate and passes 4.6; misleading/invalid output is corrected or removed. Valid markup without a Google feature may remain for a documented consumer/purpose. Feature adoption is optional and validation never guarantees display.
Tools: Schema.org validator; Rich Results Test; Search Console; Sources sheet
Notes: Purpose: search-feature eligibility; optional enhancement. C09/H05. Google FAQ rich results are no longer available, verified 2026-09-09. FAQPage remains Schema.org vocabulary; keep it only for a documented purpose rather than a Google FAQ feature/report promise. Sources: Structured-data guidelines; Google structured data features; Schema.org FAQPage; Google Search documentation updates. Source IDs: SRC007; SRC008; SRC035; SRC071.

What to do: For chosen sharing platforms, implement the basic Open Graph properties og:title, og:type, og:image and og:url. Add an accurate og:description where useful and any extra properties required by the chosen object type. Verify the actual public URL and image fetch. Configure additional platform cards only when selected, using current provider requirements.
Done when: The chosen Open Graph object has accurate required properties and accessible preview assets. Test an actual share preview where available and record the URL, result and any provider limitation. Additional platform-card requirements are verified before declaring that optional implementation Passed.
Tools: Open Graph debugger; social preview tools
Notes: Purpose: optional enhancement. Source IDs: SRC108. SRC-L01: og:type was missing from the earlier list. Current exact X Cards field requirements remain unverified because the legacy official URL redirects to a general overview; this does not establish withdrawal of the feature.

Applies to: Sites with an approved AI crawler policy
Task: Implement and verify optional AI crawler directives
What to do: Implement the approved 0.6 register in supported robots, Search Console and edge controls. Distinguish OAI-SearchBot (search), GPTBot (training) and ChatGPT-User (user fetch); Claude-SearchBot, ClaudeBot and Claude-User; and PerplexityBot versus Perplexity-User. Verify each provider's current scope and identity method. Test permitted and denied rules, label custom-UA probes as simulations, and use trusted logs for genuine requests. Keep robots accessible to compliant crawlers; never grant private access solely from a user-agent string.
Done when: Selected settings and observed behavior match the approved purposes and paths. Evidence separates rule simulations from identity-verified requests and marks unobserved behavior with an owner/follow-up. Google-Extended is tested as a product token, not a fictitious fetcher. User-directed retrieval may differ: OpenAI says robots may not apply to ChatGPT-User; Perplexity-User generally ignores it; Anthropic documents robots compliance for its bots. Robots and preview directives are not access control.
Tools: Provider documentation/register; SC effective settings; rule probes; provider identity verification; trusted logs
Review cadence: Before selected policy goes live; after provider, CDN/WAF or policy changes
Notes: Purpose: security/governance; optional enhancement. H02/D05. Preserve public-search access QA in 4.2/5.1. Apply each provider's current IP/DNS method; no generic Google identity test. For Bing, verify selected directives under Bing documentation; data-nosnippet excludes marked text from its snippets/AI summaries while retaining indexing. Sources: OpenAI crawlers; Anthropic bots; Perplexity crawlers; Bing snippet controls. Source IDs: SRC002; SRC018; SRC050; SRC084; SRC085; SRC086; SRC089.

What to do: If selected, notify currently participating IndexNow engines of added, materially updated and deleted URLs through publish/unpublish workflows. Verify host ownership, public key-file content/location and permitted URL scope. Test 200 receipt, 202 pending key validation and documented error responses; correct invalid requests and back off safely on rate limits. Check current participants instead of hard-coding an engine list. Maintain normal crawlable links and valid sitemaps, including for Google.
Done when: Add, update and deletion events send the intended in-scope URLs without persistent retry loops. Keys and host/path scope validate; receipt, pending validation and failures are logged distinctly with a follow-up owner. Successful notification is not evidence of crawling or indexing. No IndexNow integration is required if this optional scope is excluded.
Tools: IndexNow API; Bing Webmaster Tools
Review cadence: Publish/unpublish events if adopted; after key/host changes; monthly failure review
Notes: Purpose: indexing/discovery; optional enhancement. C16. Optional discovery notification, including deletions. Google discovery also uses links and other mechanisms; it is not sitemap-only. Source: IndexNow protocol documentation. Source IDs: SRC017.

Task: Product, merchant and variant configuration by scope
What to do: Record separate decisions for direct sales, product information, variants, chosen product markup, Merchant Center and checkout. Configure applicable prices, availability, currency, genuine identifiers, shipping/returns and variant URLs from the actual catalogue. Use Product snippets or merchant listing requirements for the intended surface; merchant listings require on-site purchase. Link selected feed/page/markup sources and test their agreement. Never fabricate ratings or present business testimonials as product reviews.
Done when: Every submodule decision is resolved and applicable configuration is accurate. Selected variants have stable unique identities and directly selectable URLs showing the correct state. Shipped markup passes 4.6 and multiple data sources agree. Absent checkout/feed/optional markup does not fail a module that explicitly excludes it. Review authenticity and destination rules are recorded under 3.13/7.6; no fabricated review data is accepted.
Tools: Catalogue/source data; applicable feature validator; Merchant Center if used; page/feed comparison
Notes: Purpose: search-feature eligibility; security/governance; legal/accessibility. C10. Conditional commercial accuracy and chosen-feature configuration. Product snippets, merchant listings and Merchant Center are distinct decisions. Follow the chosen single-page or multi-page ProductGroup canonical model; do not force all variants to one canonical. Sources: Product structured data; Merchant listing requirements; Product variants. Source IDs: SRC072; SRC073; SRC074; SRC083.

Task: Google Business Profile and local entity setup
What to do: Confirm Business Profile eligibility before creating or claiming a listing. Use the real business name, eligible customer-facing location or service area, correct address visibility and controlled ownership. Resolve duplicates under current location/practitioner rules. Keep hours, categories, contact details and the corresponding location page accurate. Use a tagged website link only under the measurement policy.
Done when: The eligibility decision and accountable owner are recorded. Eligible profile configuration and location-page details agree. Record actual verification state and open dependencies with an owner and next check; do not label pending verification complete. Ineligible businesses do not create a profile. Profile verification is not a universal website-launch dependency.
Tools: Google Business Profile
Review cadence: Eligibility before listing creation; launch/first 30 days follow-up; after business changes
Notes: Purpose: search-feature eligibility; optional enhancement. C11. Conditional local presence, not a universal gate. Business eligibility and exceptions follow current Google Business Profile rules. Review solicitation is governed separately under 3.13/7.6. Source: Business Profile representation guidelines. Source IDs: SRC075.

Task: Favicon, site name and search identity
What to do: Reference a stable, brand-representative square favicon from the homepage; the image may be on a CDN. Use a current supported format such as PNG/ICO, at least 8x8px and preferably larger than 48x48px. Allow Googlebot access to the homepage and Googlebot-Image access to the asset. Provide consistent WebSite name/url data on the eligible domain/subdomain homepage; reuse the existing WebSite node and align visible brand signals.
Done when: The homepage references the intended accessible favicon with a supported format and square dimensions meeting the minimum. Site-name data uses the canonical homepage URL and consistent identity. Check relevant duplicate homepages for consistent data. A separate subdirectory search site name is not promised, and lack of chosen display is not proof of invalid implementation.
Tools: Browser; Rich Results/schema validator; robots test; Search Console
Notes: Purpose: search-feature eligibility; optional enhancement. C15. Optional search-identity enhancement, not a launch requirement or ranking promise. One favicon is supported per hostname; site-name scope is domain/subdomain, with www/m generally treated as equivalent. A larger-than 48x48 favicon is a recommendation, not the 8x8 minimum. Sources: Favicon in Search; Site names. Source IDs: SRC022; SRC023.

Applies to: Sites where indexable video is a primary content asset
What to do: For selected video-search goals, provide a dedicated watch page whose main purpose is one video, with unique title/context and a prominent discoverable playable player. Check intended indexability, stable accessible thumbnails/video resources and accurate eligible VideoObject. Validate third-party embed access where used. Use a video sitemap when useful, with the watch-page URL as loc and correct video/player/thumbnail fields. Assign post-launch indexing/performance review.
Done when: Selected watch-page templates expose the intended playable main video and required accessible resources without a user action needed for discovery. Chosen markup/feed validates and agrees with the video. A product/article page with supplemental video is not claimed as a dedicated watch page. Record indexed evidence when available after launch; unavailable field data or lack of feature display is not invented as a pass.
Tools: Rich Results Test; video sitemap; Search Console; crawler
Review cadence: Before launch for video templates; review when publishing video
Notes: Purpose: search-feature eligibility; optional enhancement. H06. Conditional video-feature enhancement; adoption remains nongating. Ordinary pages with complementary video can still appear as text results. Template implementation and actual video indexing/display are separate. Source: Video SEO. Source IDs: SRC026.

Applies to: Sites with paywalled or registration-gated publishing, whether indexed or deliberately excluded
What to do: Approve the intended indexing, sampling and access model for gated publishing. Test authorized readers, logged-out clients and verified eligible crawlers against that policy, including raw/rendered responses, APIs and shared caches. For indexed paywalled content use accurate isAccessibleForFree=false; apply hasPart/cssSelector for relevant section granularity and record recommended-property decisions. Private account data requires real authorization; a Googlebot-like user agent must never grant private access.
Done when: Observed reader/crawler access and previews match approved policy. Indexed paywall markup meets required properties and chosen section selectors match actual content. Deliberately excluded publishing follows 1.8; noindex alone does not protect private data. No unauthorized private content is exposed through page, API or cache responses. Resolve and retest blocking defects before this gate passes.
Tools: URL Inspection; Rich Results/schema validator; crawler; access-control tests
Review cadence: Before gated content launches; after access-model changes
Notes: Purpose: indexing/discovery; security/governance. C17. Conditional gate protecting private data and intended search access. Keep public paid-publishing access distinct from private user accounts. Googlebot identity is verified under 1.7; labels or user-agent probes alone are insufficient. Sources: Paywalled content; Verify Google crawler requests. Source IDs: SRC028; SRC050.

Applies to: Sites selecting Discover presentation or an optional Preferred Sources user flow
Task: Discover presentation and Preferred Sources decision
What to do: Review Discover content policies for any selected content, whether or not the site is a conventional publisher. Use accurate previews and the image decisions in 2.3. Discover eligibility requires Google indexing and policy compliance, without special tags/schema. Separately check whether the domain/subdomain appears in the Preferred Sources selection tool. If chosen, implement and test a supported button/link that lets users select the actual site; do not promise a separate subdirectory source.
Done when: Selected templates have accurate previews and documented policy/image decisions. Record actual indexed evidence or a post-launch follow-up when unavailable. Preferred Sources adoption and current eligibility are recorded separately; an absent optional button or lack of source availability is not a launch failure. An implemented flow targets the intended site. Eligibility and user choice do not guarantee traffic or general ranking gains.
Tools: Search Central docs; page metadata; Search Console
Review cadence: Before selected presentation launches; first 30 days indexing follow-up; quarterly and feature changes
Notes: Purpose: search-feature eligibility; optional enhancement. H06. Optional discovery/audience module, distinct from news 2.18. Discover can include useful older and nonpublisher content. Preferred Sources is a user preference whose supported surfaces/availability need dated verification. Sources: Discover; Preferred Sources. Source IDs: SRC025; SRC032.

Applies to: Sites with hierarchical content or category structures
What to do: Provide visible, crawlable breadcrumbs representing a useful typical user path; keep linked ancestors aligned with intended canonical URLs. Do not merely mirror URL strings or invent hierarchy. Where BreadcrumbList is used, match the visible trail and validate at least two correctly ordered ListItems, names and required links. Google permits the last item to omit item; home/current-page crumbs are not automatically required.
Done when: Selected hierarchical templates have usable navigation and working canonical ancestor links. Shipped BreadcrumbList matches the visible hierarchy and relevant required properties; positions/names/links are correct on tested states. A permitted last-item link omission is accepted. Record eligibility separately from actual search display.
Tools: Rich Results Test; crawler; accessibility QA; Sources sheet
Review cadence: Before launch for hierarchical templates; after navigation changes
Notes: Purpose: indexing/discovery; search-feature eligibility. E04. Retain this existing conditional nongate control. Google's breadcrumb feature is available on desktop; that does not restrict useful on-page navigation to desktop. No guaranteed display or ranking benefit. Source: Breadcrumb navigation. Source IDs: SRC036.

Applies to: News publishers with a news programme in the release scope
Task: News publishing policy and news sitemap QA
What to do: Record publisher/company/contact details, accountable bylines and accurate original publication dates. Distinguish editorial work from advertising and disclose material sponsorship. Test current Google News policy requirements for the selected programme. If a news sitemap is used, update it as articles publish; include news metadata only for the last two days and at most 1,000 news entries per file. Validate publication name/language, original publication date and article title.
Done when: The news-policy review and tested article templates match accountable publishing and clear sponsorship. A selected news feed validates, dates are original and aged entries/news metadata are removed while appropriate normal sitemap coverage remains. An intentionally empty feed is acceptable. No news sitemap or AMP is required for ordinary websites. Unresolved applicable policy or implemented-feed defects block this module; Google News inclusion is not guaranteed.
Tools: News-policy review; article/source inspection; news sitemap validator; Search Console when available
Review cadence: Before news programme launch; each publication/feed change; first 30 days monitoring
Notes: Purpose: search-feature eligibility; security/governance. D04. Conditional news-policy/implemented-feed gate, separate from Discover 2.16. This is the site's release dependency for its chosen news programme, not a universal Google Search ranking prerequisite. Sources: Google News policies; News sitemaps. Source IDs: SRC076; SRC077.

What to do: Write unique, accurate titles and clear primary headings for priority URLs. Match the page intent and avoid arbitrary character-count rules or keyword repetition.
Done when: Every priority URL has an accurate, distinct title and primary heading; no title or heading is empty, misleading or duplicated by template error.
Tools: Screaming Frog; SERP preview
Notes: Purpose: relevance/ranking consideration. v4: meta descriptions split into a separate P1 row. Source IDs: SRC104.

What to do: Write accurate, useful descriptions for priority pages. Accept that search engines may rewrite snippets; prioritize clarity and conversion value over fixed length.
Done when: Priority pages have non-misleading descriptions and no systemic blank or duplicated template output.
Tools: Crawler; SERP preview
Notes: Purpose: optional enhancement. Source IDs: SRC105.

What to do: Link related pages using descriptive anchors when it naturally benefits the reader. Ensure priority pages are reachable in few clicks.
Done when: Priority pages reachable in few clicks; no important orphans; natural anchor text.
Tools: Screaming Frog; IA map
Notes: Purpose: indexing/discovery; relevance/ranking consideration. Replaces forced 'topic clusters' with natural contextual linking. Source IDs: SRC103.

Task: Trust, contact and required legal/consumer pages
What to do: Publish accurate About and contact information plus the privacy, terms, company, returns, accessibility or consumer-information pages required by the approved 0.9 scope. Add real authors and sources where responsibility matters.
Done when: Required pages are accurate, accessible, owned and linked from appropriate locations; claims have accountable people or organizations.
Tools: Site footer QA
Notes: Purpose: legal/accessibility; security/governance. Source IDs: SRC014; SRC033.

Task: Original content, clear answers and accountable authorship
What to do: Publish original content that meets the page's real user need with useful specifics, limits and first-hand evidence where relevant. Make answers easy to find with descriptive headings and appropriate structure. Support material claims and retain context. Show accurate authorship/review responsibility and meaningful publication/update dates where readers reasonably expect them; do not add boilerplate bylines or dates to every transactional page.
Done when: Priority content serves its stated purpose clearly and offers useful original value. Material claims have appropriate support, with consequential claims reviewed under 3.6. Authorship and dates are accurate where needed. A formatting change or AI-generated text alone does not establish quality. Applicable batch publishing is assessed separately under 3.9.
Tools: Editorial review
Review cadence: Before publication; after material content changes; periodic editorial review
Notes: Purpose: relevance/ranking consideration; security/governance. E01. Merges the previous answer-formatting requirements from 3.9. This general editorial control is P1/nongating; consequential-claim, batch and public-content risks retain their specific gates. Source: Helpful content. Source IDs: SRC033.

Applies to: YMYL, regulated, product or consequential factual claims
Task: Editorial evidence, fact-check and approval trail
What to do: Record primary sources, reviewer, approval date, material limitations and next review date for consequential claims. Use qualified legal, medical, financial or technical review when the subject requires it.
Done when: Launch claims are supportable and current; evidence and approvals are findable; unsupported testimonials, comparisons or guarantees are removed.
Tools: Editorial checklist; source log
Review cadence: Before publish; at expiry or material change
Notes: Purpose: legal/accessibility; security/governance. Source IDs: SRC033.

What to do: Define and finish the smallest set of priority landing, trust and conversion pages needed for the launch proposition. Do not block launch on an aspirational long-term editorial calendar.
Done when: Every URL marked launch-critical in the inventory has complete, approved copy, media, metadata, links and conversion path.
Tools: URL inventory; editorial tracker
Notes: Purpose: security/governance; relevance/ranking consideration. Operating design; no external ranking claim. Related controls: 0.3, 3.5, 3.6.

Task: Post-launch content production plan and cadence
What to do: Turn the keyword and intent map into a sustainable dated backlog with owners, review steps and publication dates after the minimum launch set is complete.
Done when: The next content tranche has named owners, realistic dates and an accountable backlog owner.
Tools: Content calendar; project tracker
Notes: Purpose: relevance/ranking consideration; security/governance. v4: demoted; the actual launch content set is covered by 3.7. Operating design; no external ranking claim. Related controls: 0.1, 0.2, 3.7.

Applies to: Bulk/programmatic publishing or materially AI-generated batches
Task: Batch publishing inventory, quality checks and release safeguard
What to do: Before a batch becomes indexable, record its URL inventory, legitimate user need, sources and distinct value. Define automated checks over the full batch and human review by risk, including consequential claims under 3.6. Test duplicate/template-only output, wrong entities/locations, unsupported promises, doorway patterns and factual errors. Include high-risk and edge cases in the sample. Assign a release owner, acceptance criteria and a correction/removal route; quarantine failing pages.
Done when: The inventory and review scope are complete, required checks pass and sampled defects are investigated across affected pages. Only approved passing pages enter the indexable release; failing pages remain excluded or unpublished and are retested after correction. Sources, decisions and owner are recorded. Explain creation methods where users reasonably need that context. Sampling is not a guarantee that every claim is correct.
Owner: Content owner + qualified reviewer + developer + SEO
Tools: Batch inventory; automated content checks; risk-based editorial sample; publishing controls
Review cadence: Before first batch and each material batch release; after generator/data-source changes
Notes: Purpose: security/governance. D03/E01. Conditional publishing risk gate. Old 3.9 formatting now lives in 3.5; this ID has a new criterion and purpose. Ordinary drafting uses 3.5/3.6 unless batch scope applies. Sources: Generative AI content guidance; Spam policies. Source IDs: SRC029; SRC079.

What to do: Compare a proposed page with the actual content inventory for user need, entity/product/location, substantive content and expected search role. Consolidate materially redundant pages when one stronger page serves the need. Keep distinct useful pages even when intent overlaps. After launch, use query/page evidence to investigate competition rather than assuming every overlap is harmful cannibalization.
Done when: The publish decision records why to create, update, retain or consolidate the page. Distinct entities or useful content are not merged merely for sharing an intent. Investigations use the maintained URL inventory and available search evidence; a site: query alone is not a complete inventory.
Tools: CMS/crawl inventory; content comparison; Search Console query/page evidence when available
Notes: Purpose: relevance/ranking consideration. C20. Editorial and ongoing optimization decision, not an automatic consolidation or launch rule. Sources: Helpful content; site: search limitations. Source IDs: SRC033; SRC062.

Task: Accessible content, links and media QA
What to do: Check heading meaning, descriptive link text, plain language where appropriate, table headers, image alternatives, captions/transcripts, page language and instructions that do not depend only on color, shape or position.
Done when: Priority content remains understandable and operable with images, sound or styling unavailable; media alternatives are accurate.
Tools: Editorial accessibility checklist; screen reader sampling
Notes: Purpose: legal/accessibility. Source IDs: SRC014; SRC057; SRC098.

What to do: Localize intent, terminology, currency, units, legal information, shipping/service availability, contacts and conversion copy. Do not publish raw machine translation without accountable review.
Done when: Each launch locale is reviewed by a qualified human and matches the local query, offer, legal scope and conversion journey.
Tools: Locale briefs; human QA; URL inventory
Notes: Purpose: indexing/discovery; legal/accessibility. Source IDs: SRC012; SRC013.

Applies to: Sites with public UGC, listings, third-party publishing or review collection, solicitation or display
Task: Public content, third-party publishing and review safeguards
What to do: Before public content launches, set moderation, publication/indexability thresholds and escalation owners. Review third-party provenance, purpose, responsibility, integration and actual arrangements against current spam policies; assess batches under 3.9. Qualify paid links with sponsored or accepted nofollow and handle UGC links appropriately. Before collecting/displaying reviews, shipping review markup or making the first request, approve the destination-specific rules in 7.6 and test the actual request, staff guidance and moderation flow.
Done when: Applicable publication/moderation controls work and policy defects are resolved before release. Record actual third-party arrangements and current policy version; authorship alone is not abuse. For reviews, retain genuine provenance, required disclosures, moderation/takedown evidence and approval of each destination's rules before first use. Reapprove changed platforms, incentives or request/moderation flows before use. Escalation covers relevant Search Console notices and policy review routes.
Tools: Moderation tools; crawler; Search Console; destination policy and request-flow review
Review cadence: Before public-content launch or first review collection/display/request; before material programme changes
Notes: Purpose: security/governance; legal/accessibility. H04. Verified 2026-09-09: site-reputation manual-action effects differ by searcher location. Outside the EEA they affect the identified section; inside the EEA that impact does not apply and the section may rank independently over time. No immunity or automatic outcome is promised. Integration factors are assessed together. Sources: Spam policies; Site reputation policy update; Outbound-link qualification. Source IDs: SRC029; SRC030; SRC080; SRC082; SRC083.

Task: Full staging crawl: raw HTML and rendered output
What to do: Crawl the release candidate before launch with raw-HTML and JavaScript rendering modes for status codes, titles, headings, canonicals, directives, links, assets and orphan detection. Production crawling is a separate launch-day row.
Done when: No unexplained critical difference exists between raw and rendered output; priority URLs have no broken links, missing metadata or indexation conflicts.
Tools: Screaming Frog (JS rendered); Sitebulb
Review cadence: Before launch and after big releases
Notes: Purpose: indexing/discovery. v4: split staging QA from the production crawl. Source IDs: SRC009; SRC010; SRC038; SRC039.

What to do: Compare the release candidate with 0.3 for status, directives, canonical, sitemap, links and locale. On an approved production-equivalent path, test actual cache layers cold/warm and after invalidation, relevant cookies/headers/locales, separate users and private-route authorization. Check intended crawler/visitor rules, challenges, rate limits and essential rendering resources. Record intentional staging access differences for 5.1 live confirmation.
Done when: Every launch pattern meets the approved matrix and current acceptance criteria across tested cache/access variants. No private cross-user response leak, stale indexing directive, wrong locale, or blocked required resource remains. Missing infrastructure layers are documented. Unresolved mismatches fail; an approved policy change requires matrix/criteria revision and retesting, not a Passed waiver.
Tools: Crawler export; URL matrix; cold/warm HTTP and browser probes; cache configuration; trusted logs
Notes: Purpose: indexing/discovery; security/governance. D05. This existing P0 gate owns applicable cache, WAF and privacy acceptance before cutover; 1.7 holds design evidence. It cannot prove an unobserved external crawler visit. Production path and genuine request observations follow in 5.1/6.1. Sources: HTTP caching standard; Verify Google crawler requests. Source IDs: SRC047; SRC050.

Task: Mobile content parity and critical-journey QA
What to do: Test the declared template/journey matrix on representative real phones and with a keyboard. Compare mobile/desktop primary content, headings, crawlable links, robots directives, metadata, canonicals/hreflang and relevant structured data; account for intentional separate-URL relationships. Required content/media must be available without crawler interaction. Test applicable forms, errors, labels, focus, contrast, targets, zoom, navigation and consent/banner states; link 4.4 accessibility evidence.
Done when: The complete approved matrix passes, including usable forms and keyboard/focus/error/zoom states where present. Mobile exposes equivalent essential content and correct signals/resources; no interaction-only loading, accidental mobile exclusion or blocking overlay remains. Separate mobile URLs map correctly. A different layout is acceptable when content and access requirements still pass.
Tools: Representative real phones; browser network/DOM tools; keyboard; linked accessibility evidence
Notes: Purpose: indexing/discovery; legal/accessibility. C18. Apply 1.1 rendering checks to the mobile output used for indexing. Responsive layout or an automated score alone does not prove content parity or journey access. Existing content in accessible tabs/accordions can be valid; fetching required content only after a click is different. Sources: Mobile-first indexing; Accessibility evaluation. Source IDs: SRC015; SRC058.

Applies to: All sites; conformance target follows the 0.9 scope
Task: Accessibility assessment against the approved target
What to do: Assess the version/level and scope approved in 0.9 using automated tools and knowledgeable human evaluation. Cover keyboard/focus, screen-reader use, names/roles, reflow/zoom, forms/errors, landmarks/dialogs, motion, captions and status messages as applicable. Record tested pages and complete processes, technologies, unmet criteria, severity, owners and remediation dates. Limit conclusions to the evidence actually collected.
Done when: All release-blocking access and obligation criteria in 0.9 are satisfied; unresolved blockers remain failed. The assessment records scope, methods, limitations and remaining actions. Make a conformance claim only when evidence satisfies the applicable conformance requirements, including full pages, complete processes, accessibility-supported use and non-interference. A tool score or representative sample alone is insufficient.
Tools: axe; Lighthouse; keyboard; screen reader; WCAG checklist; Sources sheet
Review cadence: Before launch and after critical UI changes
Notes: Purpose: legal/accessibility. C19. Assessment is not automatically a conformance claim. If conformance is itself a blocking obligation, missing proof remains unresolved; an owner/date is not a waiver. Legal scope is reviewed through 0.9. Sources: WCAG 2.2, section 5; Accessibility evaluation. Source IDs: SRC014; SRC015.

What to do: Run the frozen 1.5 profile on the homepage, every major launch template and relevant interactions. Record the release, tool/version, devices, network, cache state, repeated runs and agreed summary. Inspect LCP discovery, layout shifts, main-thread work, fonts and third-party code. Compare launch thresholds and diagnostic targets separately; investigate variance instead of selecting only the best run.
Done when: Every launch template passes the current approved acceptance criteria with reproducible evidence. Diagnostic overruns have impact, owner and remediation date. A failed threshold is not Passed by a signed exception. If criteria change, record approval and a new revision, then re-evaluate; stale evidence cannot authorize the revised release.
Tools: Lighthouse CI; WebPageTest; browser performance panel
Notes: Purpose: measurement; security/governance. C08. A passing lab budget is pre-launch engineering evidence, not a field CWV result. Lighthouse TBT may help diagnose responsiveness; interaction tests in a lab still do not replace real-user INP. Sources: Web Vitals metrics; Lab versus field data. Source IDs: SRC006; SRC053; SRC092.

What to do: Validate every shipped marked template in Schema.org Validator and the relevant consumer/Google feature test. Inspect rendered output and page states under 1.1. Compare entities, names, offers, availability, ratings, dates and authors with actual content/source data; investigate conflicting duplicate nodes. Apply specific feature policies and document any permitted visibility exception from its primary guidance. Separate syntax, required-property, recommendation and policy results.
Done when: No invalid or misleading shipped markup remains. Required prerequisites pass for each claimed feature, or that feature is explicitly withdrawn from the delivered matrix. Valid non-Google markup can remain with a documented purpose/owner. Recommended-property warnings have decisions rather than automatic failure. Tool success alone cannot replace content/policy review, and withdrawal is not recorded as feature eligibility.
Tools: Schema.org Validator; relevant feature test; rendered-page and source-data comparison
Notes: Purpose: search-feature eligibility; security/governance. C09. This existing gate assesses actually shipped markup, not mandatory adoption of every optional feature. Correct/remove misleading output and retest. Valid vocabulary alone does not establish Google feature eligibility. Sources: Structured-data guidelines; Google structured data features; Structured-data formats and interpretation. Source IDs: SRC008; SRC070; SRC071; SRC083.

Applies to: Sites using analytics, conversion tags or consent controls
Task: Analytics, conversion and consent QA matrix
What to do: Execute the 0.4 matrix across applicable consent states, direct/organic/campaign entry, initial loads, client routes, back/forward, forms/errors and payment returns. Repeat confirmations to test duplicate or empty/reused transaction IDs; failed/abandoned transactions must not count as completed purchases. Inspect storage and outgoing URLs, titles, event/user fields and in-scope server/vendor forwarding for prohibited data. Reconcile allowed test outcomes with the system of record.
Done when: Every required case has dated release-specific evidence matching expected collection or suppression, consent timing, values and attribution. Required events are not missing or duplicated; prohibited payloads and unintended referrals are absent. All blocking defects are corrected and retested; an owner/date alone is insufficient. Record reporting delay and unavailable diagnostics honestly; do not require unconsented users or suppressed events to appear in analytics.
Tools: Analytics debugger; Tag Assistant; network/storage tools
Notes: Purpose: measurement; legal/accessibility. C13/D06. Test actual payloads even with CMP approval or best-effort platform redaction enabled. Hashing alone does not authorize a prohibited field. Optional links and unavailable historical data are not universal gates; a missing required test remains incomplete. Sources: Consent Mode implementation timing; Analytics PII prevention; GA4 SPA measurement; GA4 transaction IDs; GA4 cross-domain measurement. Source IDs: SRC064; SRC065; SRC066; SRC067; SRC069.

Applies to: Migration / redesign / domain or URL change
Task: Migration redirect, content-parity and rollback rehearsal
What to do: Before cutover, test the full 0.8 URL inventory and redirect configuration in a controlled environment, including relevant query/host variants and assets. Validate every planned status/target automatically; compare content and SEO signals by the approved value/template matrix. Confirm destination readiness, durable GSC ownership and Change of Address eligibility. Reference the timed recovery exercise in 4.12 and recheck inherited-domain findings where applicable.
Done when: Every inventoried outcome matches the approved map: retained content has a relevant working destination, unchanged URLs remain correct, and deliberate retirements return the intended 404/410. No unintended chain, loop, missing mapping or irrelevant consolidation remains. Required parity and inherited-domain checks pass; recovery evidence meets 4.12. Live redirect activation and eligible Change of Address submission remain 5.2.
Tools: Old/new crawl diff; redirect tester; analytics/GSC baseline
Notes: Purpose: indexing/discovery; security/governance. C21/F01. Full-map status/target testing is distinct from risk-based content sampling. Approved intentional changes are recorded before testing; signing off a failed current criterion does not make it Passed. Sources: Google site moves; Change of Address. Source IDs: SRC011; SRC059.

What to do: Crawl every launch locale against 0.7/1.14 for statuses, actual content language, canonical choices, self/return hreflang, supported codes, working equivalent URLs, localized links and the chosen fallback. Test mobile/desktop locale switching without forced IP/language routing. Verify localized content and journeys against each market's approved requirements, including any documented same-language duplicate consolidation.
Done when: Intended equivalent-page clusters have correct self/return annotations and reachable targets. Distinct translations remain indexable; canonical exceptions match the documented same-language policy. Actual content is localized, switching works and fallback behavior is intentional. Missing translations are not fabricated, and unresolved routing, language or indexing conflicts fail the gate.
Tools: Crawler; hreflang validator; locale QA matrix
Notes: Purpose: indexing/discovery. C07. Validate the intended cluster, not a requirement that every URL exist in every locale. x-default is a chosen fallback, not an automatic requirement for a new page. Sources: International sites; Localized versions / hreflang. Source IDs: SRC012; SRC013.

Task: Product, checkout, variant, feed and policy QA
What to do: Use the 2.11 submodule matrix to test actual selling/catalogue surfaces. Cover representative available, sold-out, retired and variant states; crawl categories/filters under 1.12/1.13/1.15. Verify directly selected variant image/price/availability and correct cart item where sold. Test checkout only when present and feeds only when used. Compare applicable page, markup, feed and transaction totals/currency plus shipping/return policies. Investigate discrepancies against authoritative product data.
Done when: Every applicable matrix case passes with current evidence. No blocking variant crawl trap, orphan product, misleading offer/markup, inconsistent selected feed or broken chosen checkout remains. A catalogue without checkout or Merchant Center may pass its documented scope. Missing third-party approval/reporting is recorded separately from tested implementation; it is never represented as verified eligibility or successful transactions.
Tools: Catalogue-state matrix; crawler; relevant feature validator; selected feed diagnostics; checkout evidence if used
Review cadence: Before launch and catalogue platform changes
Notes: Purpose: security/governance; search-feature eligibility; legal/accessibility. C10. Conditional QA of actual commercial functions. Follow required versus recommended feature properties under 2.7/4.6. Review rules remain separate under 3.13/7.6. Sources: Product structured data; Merchant listing requirements; Product variants. Source IDs: SRC072; SRC073; SRC074.

Task: Dated pre-launch crawl, performance and visibility baseline
What to do: Archive a dated release baseline: crawl, representative lab results with the 1.5 profile, schema checks and available field data.
