Label field source, URL/origin/group/cohort, devices, window and data sufficiency. For a replaced live site also retain available rankings, traffic and top landing pages. For a first launch explicitly record which historical or field measurements do not exist.
Done when: The release-linked baseline is findable and identifies comparable measurements and limitations. Missing field or historical data is Unavailable in evidence with a reason and next review, never invented or replaced by a lab score. Post-launch comparisons identify any population, configuration or window change.
Tools: Screaming Frog export; PageSpeed; GSC export; analytics export
Notes: Purpose: measurement. C22. A new site need not possess pre-launch field history. Migration-critical baseline evidence remains scoped in 0.8/4.8. Sources: Lab versus field data; CrUX methodology and coverage; CrUX API collection window. Source IDs: SRC006; SRC054; SRC055.

What to do: Rehearse 1.17 recovery using the required backups, access and launch contacts. Restore the chosen first-launch target or existing release/data state, including the plan for post-cutover writes. Before cutover configure monitor owners, severity, routing and response targets; safely test alert delivery and escalation. Where diagnostics need logs, test approved collection, access restrictions, redaction and retention with representative records.
Done when: A recorded timed exercise restores the agreed state within recovery-time and data-loss limits; a holding mode meets its approved response/indexing behavior and duration. Contacts are current and a safe alert test reaches the monitored recipient within target. Required diagnostic records are retrievable under the approved controls. Missing or failed readiness remains HOLD; live confirmation follows in 5.5.
Tools: Runbook; hosting platform; monitoring
Notes: Purpose: security/governance. F03/F04. First launch uses the approved recoverable state or holding mode, not a nonexistent previous release. Reuse this exercise from 4.8. Preserve alert/log readiness without prescribing a universal log-retention period. Sources: Contingency planning and recovery testing; Monitoring distributed systems; Secure logging guidance. Source IDs: SRC051; SRC052; SRC063.

Task: DNS cutover and production smoke test
What to do: After cutover test the public hostname: DNS, certificates, preferred host, statuses, robots, sitemap, canonicals, assets, forms and critical journeys. Repeat 4.2's applicable cold/warm cache, invalidation, locale and private-session checks on production. Check edge challenges/rate limits and required resources. Use available provider-triggered tools and verified request logs; identify the actual crawler/fetcher category observed.
Done when: Production matches the approved matrix with no critical availability, indexing, required-access or privacy defect. Record public-path probes and verified provider requests separately. Mark an unobserved organic crawl Unavailable in evidence, with an owner and first-week follow-up in 6.1; do not claim verification or failure solely because no visit has occurred. Known required-access failures block acceptance.
Tools: Browser; HTTP probes; provider live-fetch tools; trusted edge/server logs; provider identity verification
Notes: Purpose: indexing/discovery; security/governance. D05. A spoofed user agent tests a rule only. Verify Google requests with the correct published IP category or reverse DNS plus forward match and an exact official domain boundary. A user-triggered fetch does not prove common Googlebot access. Never let bot identity bypass private-account authorization. Source: Verify Google crawler requests. Source IDs: SRC047; SRC050.

Applies to: Migration / redesign / domain or URL change
Task: Migration cutover and live redirect verification
What to do: After destination readiness and 4.8 pass, activate the approved redirects at the planned cutover. Test every inventoried live status/target and the approved content/SEO-signal sample, including host/query variants and assets. Then submit eligible Change of Address requests from the required verified source variants using the owning account. Record tool outcomes, retain domain/redirect continuity and hand monitoring to the named owner.
Done when: Live outcomes match the approved map, including intentional 404/410 retirements and relevant consolidations. No required destination, mapping or signal check fails. Eligible Change of Address requests have passed required prechecks and show the move in progress; ineligible cases have a recorded reason. Old domains/variants remain controlled and monitored under 0.8. A submission does not prove indexing or ranking recovery.
Tools: Old-site crawl; redirect tester; GSC
Review cadence: At cutover and immediately afterward; monitor through migration
Notes: Purpose: indexing/discovery; security/governance. C21. Prepare destinations before cutover; submit Change of Address only after the site is moved and redirects work. The tool's 180-day effect does not shorten the at-least-one-year redirect policy. Sources: Google site moves; Change of Address. Source IDs: SRC011; SRC059.

What to do: Crawl the public site after launch and reconcile status, robots, canonicals, metadata, internal links, sitemap URLs and rendered content against the signed release candidate and indexability matrix.
Done when: No critical production-only difference or blocked priority URL remains; exceptions have owners and immediate decisions.
Tools: Crawler; URL Inspection; crawl diff
Review cadence: Launch day and after emergency fixes
Notes: Purpose: indexing/discovery. Source IDs: SRC009; SRC010; SRC038.

Task: Verify production sitemap and priority URLs; record submission status
What to do: On the production origin, verify sitemap fetchability when a sitemap is used; otherwise confirm the approved omission and internal-discovery evidence and inspect the homepage and representative priority templates for response, crawl/indexing directives, declared canonical and rendered content. If a sitemap is used, submit it in the correctly scoped Search Console property when account/service access is available, recording actual status/time. Use live URL Inspection where available alongside direct HTTP/rendered evidence. Record unavailable access or service functions with evidence, an owner and follow-up; never infer indexed status or Google-selected canonical from a live test.
Done when: Production evidence matches the approved URL matrix for sampled launch-critical patterns and any intended sitemap is reachable; an approved omission has matching internal-discovery evidence. No known blocking live fetch/directive/canonical/content defect remains. For an implemented sitemap, submission is either evidenced or explicitly pending with an owner and next action; unavailable account/service access alone does not block. Record absent indexed data as Unavailable and follow up under 6.1. Delay or missing reports cannot excuse a demonstrated technical defect or replace required live evidence.
Tools: Google Search Console; URL Inspection
Notes: Purpose: indexing/discovery; measurement. C14 dependency. This remains a live technical gate. Recommended SC setup/submission and report availability are tracked separately and do not create an artificial indexing prerequisite. Keep declared/live and Google-selected/indexed canonical evidence separate. Sources: Search Console property types; existing live URL Inspection guidance. E02: the sitemap adoption decision follows 2.1; omission does not waive production URL tests. Source: Sitemap use decision. Source IDs: SRC009; SRC010; SRC019; SRC038; SRC087; SRC096.

What to do: Confirm the monitoring prepared in 4.12 is active on production. Check uptime, 5xx/429, DNS/SSL expiry, robots status/content, sitemap failure, canonical and unintended-noindex canaries. Include accidental robots 4xx and failed refresh/cache cases. Use a safe synthetic signal to confirm live routing and the current response runbook; do not cause a production fault.
Done when: Live canaries match the approved access/directive matrix. A safe test reaches the accountable monitored recipient within the target; severity and response steps cover the relevant URL, sitemap, robots and cache failures. Record delivery evidence and investigation ownership for anomalies.
Tools: Uptime monitor (Better Stack, Cronitor, UptimeRobot); scheduled GitHub Action; GSC alerts
Review cadence: Launch day; first-month review; approved periodic interval and after monitoring changes
Notes: Purpose: indexing/discovery; security/governance. D02/F03. Most robots 4xx except 429 mean no crawl restrictions for Google; server/network failures can interrupt crawling and retain cached rules. Pre-cutover setup/testing belongs to 4.12; this row confirms production operation. Sources: robots.txt interpretation; Monitoring distributed systems. Source IDs: SRC046; SRC050; SRC051.

Applies to: Sites using analytics or conversion measurement
Task: Live analytics and conversion smoke test
What to do: Run the approved production smoke journeys using authorized test records. Confirm expected collection or suppression for relevant consent states and transitions, page/route events, attribution, values and deduplication. Check actual network/storage behavior and appropriate recipient diagnostics; reconcile permitted transactions with the system of record. Control test-data handling and repeat any affected failures before recording the live result.
Done when: Required live cases match the approved 0.4/4.7 expectations: permitted events arrive accurately where expected, suppressed events remain absent, and denied paths work. No prohibited disclosure, duplicate purchase or required measurement failure remains. Record reporting latency and evidence limits without inferring receipt from configuration or demanding one analytics event for every action.
Tools: Analytics realtime/debug view; tag debugger; transaction records
Notes: Purpose: measurement; legal/accessibility. C12/D06. Absence can be the correct consent outcome. Workbook completion neither promises full observability nor proves legal compliance. Keep live receipt/suppression evidence separate from later aggregate reporting. Sources: Google Consent Mode; Analytics PII prevention; GA4 transaction IDs. Source IDs: SRC004; SRC065; SRC067.

Task: Record launch-owner decision and rollback window.
What to do: After reviewing the current calculated launch assessment and the production evidence, the named launch owner records GO, HOLD with remediation, or rollback for the identified release and approved scope. Record the decision time, evidence reference, remaining risks, action owners and rollback-window end. Keep the responsible people available through that window. Reassess and update the record after a failed check, remediation, rollback or material release change.
Done when: A complete dated human decision record exists and agrees with the current release, scope and evidence. A recorded GO is permitted only while the calculated final assessment is GO. Recording a HOLD or rollback can complete this administrative record; it does not change the calculated assessment.
Tools: Launch runbook; monitoring; crawl; analytics
Notes: Purpose: security/governance. Decision recording is outside its own prerequisites. Calculated readiness, owner authorization, production verification and the final human decision are separate facts. Operating design; no external ranking claim. Related controls: 4.12, 5.1, 5.2, 5.3, 5.4, 5.5, 5.6.

What to do: Where Bing is selected, verify the correctly scoped production property before or at launch and record the actual sitemap submission/processing state. Check adopted IndexNow events under 2.10. Assign first-week and first-month reviews under 6.1/6.3 for sitemap processing, crawl/index issues, search performance and relevant notifications. Check any Bing-specific directives against current Bing documentation; do not copy Google semantics by assumption.
Done when: The property and monitoring access are verified before marking this setup Passed; otherwise keep it unfinished with a reason, owner and next action. Record actual submission receipt and processing separately from indexed status. First-week and first-month checks have dates and owners and feed the reporting review. Optional AI citation reporting is handled separately under 6.4.
Tools: Bing Webmaster Tools
Review cadence: Before or at launch if selected; first week and first month; thereafter via 6.3
Notes: Purpose: measurement. C23. Conditional monitoring, not a search-ranking or universal launch requirement. Source: Bing AI Performance announcement and Bing sitemap guidance. Source IDs: SRC089; SRC091.

What to do: Compare submitted, crawled, canonical and indexed URLs by template; inspect priority pages and assign causes/owners for exclusions. For Google indexed URL Inspection, compare selected and declared canonicals against the approved matrix, recording indexed-data time, current live evidence and whether the report predates release. Investigate material mismatches without treating intentional consolidation as failure. Where Bing is selected, review its sitemap processing and crawl/index issues in the first week and first month with engine-specific evidence.
Done when: Known blockers and material canonical/indexing mismatches have investigation, fix and retest owners. Review available indexed evidence; record missing or lagging data as Unavailable with the next check date, separately for each engine. Do not invent an indexed result or treat this follow-up as a retrospective day-one indexing prerequisite.
Tools: Search Console indexed/live URL Inspection; Bing tools where selected; URL matrix
Notes: Purpose: indexing/discovery; measurement. D05 follow-up: in the first week, review unobserved crawler cases from 5.1 using correctly verified request logs and available search-tool evidence. Record the crawler category, URL/time/status, method and any access failure; if still unobserved, keep that evidence Unavailable with an owner and next date. A live user-triggered fetch is not proof of a normal indexing crawl. Source: Verify Google crawler requests. Source IDs: SRC010; SRC019; SRC091.

What to do: Review available field LCP, INP and CLS at p75, separating mobile and desktop. Name the source and actual URL, origin, Search Console group or first-party RUM cohort; do not present one as another. Record the collection window, sample/coverage limits and release timing. Good boundaries are LCP <=2.5 s, INP <=200 ms and CLS <=0.1. Use lab and relevant RUM evidence to diagnose regressions and assign actions.
Done when: Available metrics have a named population/window/device segment and correct grade. Missing or insufficient metrics are Unavailable in evidence with an owner and next review, not Passed or Failed. Regressions have impact, action owners and retest dates. Completing this review does not claim that the site has Good field CWV.
Tools: PageSpeed Insights / CrUX API; Search Console CWV groups; approved first-party RUM; lab diagnostics
Notes: Purpose: measurement; relevance/ranking consideration. C22. CrUX API/PSI rolling collection periods span 28 days, but a newly launched page may contribute fewer observed days. First-party RUM can start at launch with its own stated window/sample and approved collection scope. Origin/group data is not a per-template guarantee; do not average percentiles into one score. Status records review completion only. Sources: Web Vitals metrics; CrUX API collection window; CrUX methodology and coverage; Search Console CWV groups. Source IDs: SRC053; SRC054; SRC055; SRC056; SRC092; SRC097.

What to do: Track selected engines' queries, clicks, crawl/index health and content gaps, plus available conversions and field CWV under their approved measurement scopes. For Bing selected in 5.8, include first-week and first-month sitemap, crawl/index, search-performance and notification checks. Define anomaly thresholds, denominators, reporting lag and the investigation owner. Preserve engine/report/time-window labels; keep AI impressions, citations and referral sessions separate under 6.4.
Done when: A dated reporting rhythm and actionable thresholds exist. Each selected engine's checks have evidence or explicit Unavailable/pending states, owners and next dates. Material anomalies have documented dispositions. Missing data is not silently converted to zero, and incompatible engine or AI metrics are not added together as a single visibility score.
Tools: Selected search-engine tools; approved analytics; field-performance sources; issue/evidence log
Notes: Purpose: measurement. Source IDs: SRC019; SRC053; SRC091.

Applies to: Sites with available AI-search reporting or meaningful AI referrals
What to do: Record actual Google Search Generative AI report availability and earliest data date. Use its impressions for AI Overviews/AI Mode with property/page aggregation, device/country, date range and reporting time zone; Discover uses a separate report and Search Labs is excluded. Preserve missing-data markers before export, which may convert them to zeros. If selected, keep Bing AI citation counts and grounding-query samples separate. Measure identifiable AI referral sessions only under the approved analytics scope; optional dated prompt spot checks are anecdotal.
Done when: The baseline names each report, metric, scope, period and availability limits. Google AI impressions are not clicks, CTR, rankings or all-provider visibility; Bing citations are not those metrics either. Referral sessions have their own attribution limits. Do not sum incompatible datasets or equate chart/table totals with different aggregation. Record unavailable/insufficient data explicitly and do not fabricate pre-availability history. Prompt examples are not representative coverage estimates.
Tools: SC Search/Discover AI reports where available; optional Bing AI Performance; approved referral analytics
Notes: Purpose: measurement. H01/C23. Checked 2026-09-09: Google announces worldwide AI-report rollout as of 2026-08-31, while its help still lists account/data caveats. Verify actual availability. Bing's cited announcement labels AI Performance public preview; verify current account features and metric scope. Sources: Search AI performance report; Bing AI Performance. Source IDs: SRC034; SRC090.

What to do: Review GSC Security Issues, Manual Actions and alerts; maintain the CMS/dependency patching owner and investigate unexpected published URLs. Record report scope, access limitations and findings with incident owners, remedies and next checks. Use site: only as a supplemental discovery aid. Recheck after launch, on alerts and after material incidents; inherited-domain checks also belong before cutover in 0.8.
Done when: Required reports were actually reviewed, findings were investigated and actions/escalation are recorded. Missing access is explicit and the affected review stays incomplete. Critical incidents remain open until verified remediation; review completion does not mean the site has no issues. Do not infer a clean site from absent search results or a short sample of affected URLs.
Tools: Search Console reports/alerts; CMS and dependency security tooling; incident log
Notes: Purpose: security/governance. F01. The Status records completion of this monitoring review, not a security certification or absence of manual actions. Preserve incident outcomes separately and reopen affected release controls. Sources: Manual actions; Security issues; site: operator limitations. Source IDs: SRC060; SRC061.

Applies to: Migration / redesign / domain or URL change
What to do: Monitor old high-value URLs, server 404s, redirect chains, crawl rate, indexed old/new URLs, traffic and ranking transitions. Correct missed mappings without redirecting irrelevant URLs to the homepage.
Done when: Material missed redirects and parity defects are fixed; visibility changes are explained and monitored through stabilization.
Tools: Server logs; crawler; GSC; analytics
Review cadence: Daily first week; weekly through day 30
Notes: Purpose: indexing/discovery; measurement. Source IDs: SRC011; SRC041; SRC042.

Applies to: Sites using analytics or conversion measurement
What to do: Compare analytics conversions and revenue with forms, CRM, orders or other systems of record. Investigate duplicates, missing events, attribution changes and consent-related gaps.
Done when: Material differences are quantified, explained and assigned; dashboards use documented definitions.
Tools: Analytics; CRM/order system; reconciliation sheet
Notes: Purpose: measurement. Source IDs: SRC004; SRC067; SRC069.

What to do: Check product/feed/rich-result errors, variant canonicals, hreflang clusters, locale indexation and localized conversions using the reports relevant to the deployed features.
Done when: Errors and coverage gaps have owners, priority and retest evidence; no template-wide regression remains unexplained.
Tools: Search Console; Merchant Center; crawler; analytics
Notes: Purpose: search-feature eligibility; indexing/discovery; measurement. Source IDs: SRC008; SRC013; SRC073; SRC074.

Applies to: Sites investigating material inbound-link risk or inherited link schemes
Task: Link-risk triage and conditional disavow response
What to do: Investigate material inbound-link concerns using actual link history and Search Console evidence. Consider disavow only when a considerable number of artificial, spammy or low-quality links exist AND they have caused or are likely to cause a manual action. Attempt removal where feasible first. An alleged attack or toxicity score alone is insufficient. Before an approved upload, confirm ownership of the intended URL-prefix property, preserve its current list and review the exact replacement; Domain properties are unsupported.
Done when: Record the evidence, qualified decision and reason for acting or taking no action; most sites need no disavow. Any approved submission meets both threshold conditions, documents feasible removal attempts and targets the correct property without unintentionally losing prior entries. Keep the submitted version and follow-up record; processing is not immediate and recovery is not guaranteed. No upload is required merely to pass this control.
Tools: Search Console Links/manual actions; link history; disavow tool only when justified
Review cadence: Incident-driven from pre-launch onward; revisit when link-risk evidence changes
Notes: Purpose: security/governance; optional enhancement. C24. Optional incident response, moved to Ongoing while retaining stable ID 6.8. Do not infer a manual-action risk from third-party toxicity scores alone. Source: Disavow links to your site. Source IDs: SRC081.

Task: Ongoing monitoring, incident ownership and response SLA
What to do: Maintain alerts for availability, robots/noindex/canonical changes, sitemap failures, organic/conversion anomalies, security issues and expiring DNS/SSL dependencies. Keep severity, owner, response time and rollback steps current.
Done when: Use the single alert-test schedule in 5.5: before launch, the first-month operational review, the approved periodic interval and after monitoring changes. Retain delivered-alert evidence and incident timestamps, owners, decisions, remediation and prevention follow-up in the review history.
Tools: Monitoring; Search Console; analytics; incident log
Review cadence: Continuous monitoring; approved alert-test schedule in 5.5
Notes: Purpose: security/governance. Reuse current 4.12 readiness and 5.5 live evidence where relevant; keep distinct pre-cutover, live and recurring outcomes. Record affected incidents as Reopened and append retest outcomes. Source IDs: SRC051; SRC052.

What to do: Review pages losing clicks, outdated facts, cannibalization, weak conversions, broken links, and thin content. Refresh/merge/prune with reason.
Done when: Dated audit log has decisions per declining URL.
Tools: GSC; crawl
Notes: Purpose: relevance/ranking consideration. Source IDs: SRC033.

What to do: At the approved periodic interval, crawl the full intended inventory and compare it with the prior run. Review response codes, indexability, links, canonical and sitemap signals, structured data and current field-performance evidence. Run scoped lab checks where useful; a lab result is not a field Core Web Vitals result. Use 7.4 for affected-release checks.
Done when: Retained dated full-inventory comparisons, appropriately labelled field/lab findings and owned regression tickets exist. Record the latest outcome and next review UTC in review history; reopen affected controls and verify remediation.
Tools: Screaming Frog; PageSpeed; Rich Results Test
Review cadence: Approved periodic interval; record next review UTC
Notes: Purpose: indexing/discovery; measurement. Complements content review 7.2 and release-scope checks 7.4. Reuse current artifacts when their scope and criterion match; do not require identical reruns for each checklist row. Source IDs: SRC006; SRC038; SRC053.

Task: Release-based SEO, accessibility and performance regression review
What to do: Before each material template, CMS, navigation, tracking, CDN or design-system release, identify affected controls and record reopening for the target release. Run the relevant crawl, lab-budget, structured-data, analytics and accessibility checks before cutover, then confirm production-only outcomes after release. Keep first-month/periodic field measurements separate from immediate lab acceptance.
Done when: Each material release has an affected-control inventory, retained pre-release and production-confirmation results, evidence references and owned follow-up. Current applicable launch gates meet their existing stage-specific criteria; a later incident or regression reopens affected controls. Append retests to the review history.
Tools: Release checklist; CI; crawler; test tools
Review cadence: Before each material release; production confirmation after cutover; after relevant incidents
Notes: Purpose: indexing/discovery; legal/accessibility; security/governance. Reuse 4.12 recovery rehearsal and relevant 5.5 monitoring evidence without duplicating exercises. 7.3 remains the periodic full-inventory review. Source IDs: SRC006; SRC015.

Task: Digital PR and legitimate link earning
What to do: Earn relevant mentions through original research, tools, expertise, partnerships, communities and legitimate press. Measure relevance, referral value and durable brand impact rather than raw link count.
Done when: An owned outreach plan and documented relevant wins exist without paid or manipulative link schemes.
Tools: CRM; GSC links
Notes: Purpose: relevance/ranking consideration. Source IDs: SRC029; SRC030; SRC033.

Task: Off-page link, review and reputation governance
What to do: Use the 3.13-approved rules before each review programme starts or changes. For Google Maps/Business Profile, forbid incentives, positive-only solicitation/review gating, pressure, demands for specific content or staff names, staff review quotas and benefits for removing/changing negative reviews. Invite honest genuine feedback without influencing it. For other destinations, verify their rules and applicable law before any incentive; require necessary disclosure and no sentiment condition. Prohibit ranking-manipulation link schemes; qualify commercial/UGC links appropriately and monitor material reviews, unlinked mentions, profile/citation accuracy and genuine reputation issues.
Done when: Record each active destination, policy date, accountable owner, request/moderation workflow and recheck date. Review requests and staff guidance match the approved rules. Markup describes genuine, visible, eligible reviews of the actual item; do not aggregate other sites' ratings. Self-serving LocalBusiness/Organization reviews, including embedded widgets, are ineligible for review stars. Assess Product reviews separately under 2.11/4.6; never relabel business testimonials as product reviews. Material violations trigger pause, correction and renewed approval before resuming.
Tools: Brand monitoring; review platforms; link reports
Review cadence: Before first programme via 3.13; monthly monitoring; before policy, supplier, incentive or flow changes
Notes: Purpose: security/governance; legal/accessibility. F02/H03. Google Maps prohibits incentives even with disclosure. Other platforms and legal duties vary; disclosure is not permission. Review-feature eligibility is separate from ordinary reputation management. Sources: Maps review policy; Review snippet guidelines; Spam policies. Source IDs: SRC029; SRC082; SRC083.

What to do: Sample new and high-traffic templates with automated and manual checks; review keyboard, screen-reader, zoom/reflow, forms, dialogs, media alternatives and content patterns. Track remediation by severity.
Done when: Dated samples and issue trends exist; critical barriers trigger immediate incident handling.
Tools: axe; keyboard; screen reader; WCAG checklist
Review cadence: Quarterly and after major UI changes
Notes: Purpose: legal/accessibility. Source IDs: SRC014; SRC015.

Applies to: Sites needing crawl or incident log diagnostics
What to do: Where scale, complex crawl paths or symptoms justify analysis, review approved logs for verified crawler fetches, response errors, throttling, blocked resources and wasted discovery. Keep custom-user-agent claims separate from verified requests. Use the collection/redaction/retention policy prepared in 4.12; restrict access and investigate unexpected gaps or sensitive fields.
Done when: The review identifies its time window, verified crawler category, significant errors/waste and any data limits. Actions have owners and next checks. Sensitive data and credentials are excluded or protected under the approved policy. No need for detailed analysis is recorded explicitly rather than inventing results.
Tools: Server logs; analyzer
Review cadence: At the approved interval or on crawl/incident symptoms
Notes: Purpose: measurement; security/governance. F03/D05. Detailed analysis is conditional; required collection must exist before the incident. Minimize diagnostic data, apply access controls and honor approved retention/deletion obligations. Sources: Verify Google crawler requests; Secure logging guidance. Source IDs: SRC050; SRC052.

Applies to: Sites using structured data, internationalization or merchant feeds
What to do: Review template accuracy, relevant feature/report changes, visible-content parity, hreflang coverage and merchant feed/page discrepancies. Revalidate affected output after schema, locale, CMS or catalogue changes. Update the 2.7 consumer/feature matrix and owners when support changes; distinguish removed feature eligibility from vocabulary validity.
Done when: Required current reviews are complete and unexplained template defects have been resolved or retained as open actions with owners. Invalid/misleading markup is corrected or removed. Retain or retire valid non-feature markup deliberately based on purpose and maintenance cost; do not delete it merely because a Google feature/report ended. Keep missing reports explicit and reopen affected release checks.
Tools: Search Console; validators; Merchant Center; crawler
Notes: Purpose: search-feature eligibility; indexing/discovery. C09/H05. Review completion is not proof of rich-result display or ranking improvement. Retain the existing hreflang and merchant checks; feature withdrawal must not be mistaken for a vocabulary-wide prohibition. Sources: Structured-data guidelines; Google structured data features; Google Search documentation updates; Schema.org FAQPage. Source IDs: SRC007; SRC008; SRC035; SRC071.

Task: Security, manual actions and dependency maintenance
